#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>OfficeHQ</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <app-root></app-root>
  </body>
</html>

content.text:
Sign-in and sheet loading now work on the single screen at `/`, and `bin/e2e` passes.

**How it behaves**
- You sign in by typing a name (no password). The name then shows as `current-user`, and the browser sends it as an `X-User` header on every request after that.
- You load a sheet by typing its id. The active id shows as `sheet-current-id`. An id that's never been used starts a new empty sheet; loading an id again reads it fresh from the store. Two users loading the same id get the same sheet.
- If a form is refused (a blank name, or a sheet id with characters other than letters, digits, `-` or `_`), it shows `signin-error` or `sheet-error`. The error goes away as soon as you edit the form or submit it again.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new database migration, `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__sheet.sql`, adds a `sheet` table (id, who created it, when).
- **Server:**
  - `POST /api/session` handles sign-in by name.
  - `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load` returns the sheet, or creates it if it doesn't exist yet. If two users create the same new sheet at the same moment, both get that one sheet.
  - The code is in the new `session/` and `sheet/` packages.
- **Front end:** two services in `core/` hold the signed-in user and the active sheet, plus two small form components, `features/session/signin.ts` and `sheet-picker.ts`. The home page shows the sign-in form until someone signs in, then the sheet picker.

**Decisions for you**
- **Sign-in only lasts for the page.** The name isn't saved anywhere, so reloading the browser signs you out. The test doesn't need more, but you may want it kept.
- **The server doesn't check who's signed in.** It accepts whatever name arrives in the `X-User` header. With no passwords that's arguably fine, but anyone calling the API directly can claim any name.
- **No audit records are written.** The spec doesn't expect any for this change.

Sign-in and sheet loading now work on the single screen at `/`, and `bin/e2e` passes.

**How it behaves**
- You sign in by typing a name (no password). The name then shows as `current-user`, and the browser sends it as an `X-User` header on every request after that.
- You load a sheet by typing its id. The active id shows as `sheet-current-id`. An id that's never been used starts a new empty sheet; loading an id again reads it fresh from the store. Two users loading the same id get the same sheet.
- If a form is refused (a blank name, or a sheet id with characters other than letters, digits, `-` or `_`), it shows `signin-error` or `sheet-error`. The error goes away as soon as you edit the form or submit it again.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new database migration, `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__sheet.sql`, adds a `sheet` table (id, who created it, when).
- **Server:**
  - `POST /api/session` handles sign-in by name.
  - `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load` returns the sheet, or creates it if it doesn't exist yet. If two users create the same new sheet at the same moment, both get that one sheet.
  - The code is in the new `session/` and `sheet/` packages.
- **Front end:** two services in `core/` hold the signed-in user and the active sheet, plus two small form components, `features/session/signin.ts` and `sheet-picker.ts`. The home page shows the sign-in form until someone signs in, then the sheet picker.

**Decisions for you**
- **Sign-in only lasts for the page.** The name isn't saved anywhere, so reloading the browser signs you out. The test doesn't need more, but you may want it kept.
- **The server doesn't check who's signed in.** It accepts whatever name arrives in the `X-User` header. With no passwords that's arguably fine, but anyone calling the API directly can claim any name.
- **No audit records are written.** The spec doesn't expect any for this change.
